title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution and Obfuscation Playbook
source: CISA / NSA / ASD Guidance 'Keeping PowerShell: Security Measures to Use and Mitigate' & MITRE ATT&CK
content:
### 1. OVERVIEW & DETECTION
PowerShell is frequently abused by threat actors for living-off-the-land (LotL) execution, memory-only script injection, and environment reconnaissance. Detection indicators include:
- Command lines containing base64 encoded flags: -EncodedCommand, -enc, -e, -ec.
- Execution bypass parameters: -ExecutionPolicy Bypass, -ep bypass, -WindowStyle Hidden, -w hidden, -NoProfile, -nop, -NonInteractive.
- Download cradles and in-memory execution: Net.WebClient.DownloadString, Invoke-WebRequest, Invoke-Expression, IEX, [System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load.
- AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface) and ETW (Event Tracing for Windows) tampering or patching in memory.

### 2. EVIDENCE & ARTIFACTS TO EXAMINE
- Windows PowerShell Event Logs: Event ID 4104 (ScriptBlock Logging - captures full deobfuscated payload executed in runtime), Event ID 4103 (Module Logging), Event ID 400 (Engine State).
- PowerShell Transcription Logs: Text files generated when Transcription is enabled via Group Policy, capturing all interactive and non-interactive input/output.
- Process Lineage: Windows Event ID 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1 examining parent processes such as winword.exe, excel.exe, outlook.exe, w3wp.exe, or sqlservr.exe directly spawning powershell.exe or pwsh.exe.
- Console History: %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\PSReadLine\ConsoleHost_history.txt for interactive command execution.

### 3. INVESTIGATION & TRIAGE
- Deobfuscation Analysis: Base64-decode encoded command strings to reveal destination URLs, secondary staged payloads, or API hooking calls.
- Parent Process Correlation: Assess whether the PowerShell invocation originated from legitimate administrator automation (e.g., SCCM, Ansible, scheduled maintenance) or unexpected Office binaries / public web services.
- Network Activity Correlation: Cross-reference the timestamp of execution against proxy logs or firewall flows to identify external IPs contacted during download cradle invocations.

### 4. CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES
- Terminate Active Processes: Kill running malicious PowerShell processes and associated child processes via EDR or Task Manager.
- Network Isolation: Isolate the affected endpoint to prevent lateral movement via PowerShell Remoting (WinRM, port 5985/5986) or WMI (port 135/445).
- Account Lockdown: Disable or reset credentials for any user account under which the unauthorized script executed.

### 5. ERADICATION, RECOVERY & REMEDIATION
- Enforce Constrained Language Mode (CLM): Configure PowerShell Constrained Language Mode via AppLocker or Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) to restrict COM object creation and direct .NET type reflection.
- Enable Comprehensive Logging: Mandate GPO deployment of PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104) and Transcription.
- Restrict PowerShell Remoting: Restrict WinRM listener access to authorized jump hosts and management subnets only.
- Upgrade to PowerShell v7+: Deprecate and remove PowerShell v2.0 (which lacks modern security logging and AMSI hooks).
